title: What Isnt Coachable
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article tackles a question leaders rarely stop to ask directly: which traits are genuinely coachable, and which aren't worth the time investment to try to change. While acknowledging the debate is unsettled and that people can make small gains even in hard-to-change areas over long stretches of time, the piece offers a working shortlist of largely uncoachable qualities — self-awareness, intrinsic motivation, creativity, resilience, judgment, and performance anxiety. The author frames the real cost of getting this wrong as wasted time and mutual frustration when a leader keeps coaching toward a trait that coaching structurally can't move. The piece closes by urging leaders to decide, in advance, what belongs on their own uncoachable list so they can redirect their limited coaching time toward areas more likely to yield growth.
points: The essay offers a specific, named shortlist of largely uncoachable traits (self-awareness, intrinsic motivation, creativity, resilience, judgment, performance anxiety) rather than a vague claim that 'some things can't be taught.'
It explicitly frames the cost of misjudging coachability as wasted leadership time and mutual frustration, giving the distinction practical stakes.
It preserves nuance by acknowledging small long-term gains are possible even in nominally uncoachable areas, while still arguing coaching isn't the mechanism that produces them.
Its closing challenge — decide your own uncoachable list in advance — turns the essay into an actionable planning exercise rather than a passive read.
quotes: Exactly what is coachable, and what is uncoachable? While there are no definitive answers to these questions, the consensus among leadership experts is that most skills, traits, and aptitudes are coachable.
But that doesn’t mean it is a good use of time for leaders to coach others while hoping for change regarding a quality that is unlikely, if not impossible, to improve.
Great leaders recognize the transformative power of coaching while also accepting that some skills and traits are uncoachable.
Those with extensive coaching experience offer the following traits and skills as largely uncoachable: Self-awareness, Intrinsic Motivation, Creativity, Resilience, Judgment, and Performance Anxiety.
Decide before you invest the time to push an immovable rock uphill in a storm.
